text:
By Trevor Horn ,
8 hours ago
BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) -- It’s down to the final three weeks of the regular season and we have some very interesting league match-ups this week heading in.
No league race has been decided around Kern County, and plenty of local programs are vying for top seeds in the Central Section playoffs that will be announced on Oct. 31.
Fun times to be had.
Let’s dive in.
Thurs, Oct. 15
Tehachapi (2-5, 0-1) at Highland (3-4, 0-2)
Last week: No. 6 BCHS d. Tehachapi, 38-0; No. 11 Independence d. Highland, 28-7
For Highland’s sake, the hardest part of the Valley League slate for the Scots is over after taking on No. 6 Bakersfield Christian and No. 11 Independence in losses the first two weeks of league play.
As for Tehachapi, the Warriors have also played Bakersfield Christian, but still have Independence and Ridgeview (6-1) left after this week.
Highland senior do-it-all RJ Davenport is putting together a season that rivals some of the best in Kern County this season, scoring 11 touchdowns on offense, defense and special teams. It’s been impressive what he has done for the Scots.
The season for the Warriors might have been expected with a smaller roster than usual at Tehachapi and losing a big senior class and a record-setting quarterback, as well.
“Mountain Football” doesn’t stay down long.
Trevor’s pick: Highland 35, Tehachapi 7
Mira Monte (4-3, 1-1) at Arvin (1-5, 1-1)
Last week: McFarland d. Mira Monte, 7-0; Arvin d. West, 21-14
A big sigh of relief in Arvin after the Bears won the first game of the season in a 21-14 win against West last week, snapping a 10-game losing streak.
Alejandro Osorio rushed for 142 yards and two touchdowns for Arvin last week.
On the other side, Mira Monte’s four-game game win streak came to a halt in a 7-0 loss to McFarland at home last week.
The Lions had the ball three times against the Cougars inside the 10-yard line and couldn’t get any points across.
A big game on a Thursday night as Arvin needs to win two of the final three to be eligible for the playoffs and the Lions need a win to try and stay near the top of Division VI in the section with the playoffs right around the corner.
Trevor’s pick: Mira Monte 14, West 7
Fri, Oct. 16
No. 5 Bakersfield (5-2, 1-1) at Centennial (1-5, 0-2)
Last week: BHS d. Stockdale, 63-0; No. 7 Garces d. Centennial, 35-0
Last week, BHS righted the ship with a blowout, 63-0, win over Stockdale. The Drillers did everything right against the Mustangs in all three phases.
Damir Lomax rushed for 117 yards and two scores while D’Mariae Lee added two more rushing touchdowns while Kaiden Bolden scored a rushing, receiving and defensive touchdown for BHS.
Centennial is coming off a 35-0 loss at home to No. 7 Garces last week in the most lopsided loss of the season for the Golden Hawks. Each of the previous four losses for Centennial were decided in the fourth quarter, but last week had a fourth quarter running clock.
Trevor’s pick: BHS 42, Centennial 14
No. 6 BCHS (5-1, 2-0) at Ridgeview (6-1, 1-1)
Last week: BCHS d. Tehachapi, 38-0; Ridgeview d. Golden Valley, 46-18
In his first and only game back at Tehachapi as an opponent after breaking the single-season passing record for the Warriors in 2025, BCHS senior signal caller Colton Michael had himself a fantastic night at Coy Burnett Stadium.
Michael was 20 of 23 passing for 224 yards and four touchdowns. RJ Shehee (110 receiving yards) and Owen Yurosek both caught two touchdown passes from Michael.
This is a big one.
BCHS and Independence sit alone atop the league standing while Ridgeview hopes to stay in the title hunt this week.
Darryon Casteel continues to shine for the Wolf Pack. The senior quarterback threw for two scores and ran another in as Ridgeview beat Golden Valley 46-18 in a non-league, cross-over game last week.
The Eagles should edge out the Wolf Pack here, but could very well be a contest late.
Trevor’s pick: BCHS 28, Ridgeview 14
No. 7 Garces (*2-5, 2-0) at Frontier (1-6, 1-1)
Last week: Garces d. Centennial, 35-0; No. 13 Liberty d. Frontier, 38-26
Got to give it up to Garces. The Rams have really come to play in River League action with a gritty 20-16 win over BHS and then dominating Centennial last week, 35-0.
A lot of a talk is about the offense for Garces, but the defense has been stellar, as well.
Jackson Parker and Mahden Meyers led the way with eight tackles each against Centennial while the Rams had seven tackles for loss and an interception by Isaiah Flores.
Frontier has been on the losing end of six games now, all at the hands of teams either in the top-25 in the section or undefeated from NorCal.
And a bright spot for the Titans through this gauntlet of a season is the emergence of seniors Drake Hults (1,218 passing yards, 14 TDs) and receiver Tyler Jenkins (864 rec yards, 9 TDs), including a second 200-plus yard receiving performance by Jenkins last week in the loss to Liberty.
The Rams are arguably one of the top teams in the section and have a shot at the D-IA playoffs, but a lot has to work for that to happen. If not, a top seed in D-II could also be a landing spot for Garces if the team wins out.
Should be a shootout with Garces victorious once again.
Trevor’s pick: Garces 42, Frontier 21
No. 11 Independence (5-1, 2-0) at North (4-3, 2-0)
Last week: Independence d. Highland, 27-8; North d. East, 12-7
North High head coach Adam Levinson knows the Independence offense and defense like the back of his hand. Why? Because the third-year head coach for the Stars not only was an assistant for Falcons’ head coach Paul Golla at BHS and Garces before becoming a head coach for the first time in 2024, he also played for close friend at BHS in Golla’s first year in 2005.
North is coming off a gutsy 12-7 win over East where Caden Haner picked off a pass at the goal line with 8 minutes, 26 seconds left on the clock as the Stars’ offense held on the remainder.
On the other side, Independence overcame three early turnovers to defeat Highland 27-8.
Christian Meyers had three sacks against the Scots and has 7.5 in the past two games for the Falcons.
The Falcons offense was a ground-and-pound affair last week with Rayland Denweed leading the way with 125 rushing yards while Jakhi Ervin scored twice on the ground.
In what likely will be the only meeting in the foreseeable future between these two coaches and great friends, the mentor will get the better of the moment before a long-waited embrace at midfield following. Sometimes it’s bigger than football.
Trevor’s pick: Independence 28, North 7
Stockdale (1-6, 0-2) at No. 13 Liberty (5-2, 2-0)
Last week: BHS d. Stockdale, 63-0; Liberty d. Frontier, 38-26
Liberty had a dogfight last week against a Frontier squad eager to show their mite. But a 21-point second quarter for the Patriots was too much for the Titans to overcome as Liberty looks to remain undefeated in league play at home against Stockdale knowing that Garces is looking next week.
Leon Denweed had a big night for Liberty over Frontier with a whopping 28 carries for 143 yards and a touchdown. Luke Valverde threw for 112 yards with touchdown passes to Jonah Manning and Ryker Maes-Morrison with Gavin Williams out-of-state in a national baseball showcase.
Bad news for the Mustangs, Williams is back this week and Liberty has too much talent in this one to fall prey to a trap game.
Trevor’s pick: Liberty 42, Stockdale 7
Delano (1-6, 0-2) at No. 14 Shafter (6-1, 2-0)
No. 18 Kennedy d. Delano, 63-6; Shafter d. Taft, 56-7
The South Sequoia League win streak for Shafter is quite impressive knowing that during the time the Generals, since the end of 2022, two league opponents have played for a state championship with Wasco losing the CIF State D-6AA title in 2023 and Kennedy winning the D-3A state championship last December.
Wasco was the last team to beat Shafter in a league game on Oct. 28, 2022 in a 41-35 loss for the Generals. That season, Shafter, themselves, played in, and lost to Orland in D-5A state finals.
Since the start of the 2023 season, Shafter is 38-6 and have won 17 consecutive league games.
This season, as solid as the offense has been, the story for Shafter this fall is the defense. Outside of the 41-38 to still-undefeated Tulare Western, the Generals have given up just 28 points in the six wins including just one touchdown in the two league wins over Chavez and Taft.
Shafter’s biggest hurdles this season in that win streak are still to come with Kennedy at home Oct. 23 and the 99th annual showdown at Wasco on Oct. 30.
Delano will have two more chances to get a league win against Chavez or Taft the final two weeks, it just won’t be this week against a team that likely could be the No. 1 seed in D-IV.
Trevor’s pick: Shafter 49, Delano 6
No. 18 Kennedy (6-1, 2-0) at Wasco (4-3, 2-0)
Last week: Kennedy d. Delano, 63-6; Wasco d. Chavez, 33-13
Speaking of great defenses. Kennedy scored four defensive touchdowns, including three interceptions returned for touchdowns by Isaiah Feathers, Jordan Palomo and Jorge Avila. Yes, those were, in fact, not offense scores but three pick-6s by the three of the Thunderbirds top offensive players.
Feathers also scored on a fumble recovery and scored a rushing touchdown just to keep everyone honest.
Trevor’s pick: Kennedy 35, Wasco 21
East (4-3, 1-1) at Foothill (7-0, 0-2)
Last week: North d. East, 12-7; Foothill d. South, 40-7
Foothill has been dominant on offense and defense all season.
No team in program history has gone 10-0.
East will not go down without a fight. The Blades’ interior defense looked solid against North in a 12-7 to the Stars. While the offense was able to muster just one score last week, this week will come down to the defense for East to try and slow down the Trojans.
Trevor’s pick: Foothill 35, East 14
Taft (5-2, 0-2) at Chavez (4-3, 0-2)
Last week: No. 14 Shafter d. Taft, 56-7; Wasco d. Chavez, 33-13
Tough ending to the game last week for Friday. A player for the Titans was taken away on an ambulance after experiencing a medical emergency on the sideline in the fourth quarter. The game was stopped mid-way through the fourth with Wasco earning the victory.
A rallying cry for Chavez and the players this week back at home against a Taft team ready to not play a team ranked in the top-20.
Following an impressive 5-0 start to the season, the Wildcats lost in blowouts to Shafter and Kennedy to open up league play.
This game should be much more balanced for both squads and the re-emergence of Taft’s running back Joe Weber should happen here.
Trevor’s pick: Taft 28, Chavez 21
Golden Valley (2-5, 0-1) at South (2-5, 0-2)
Last week: Ridgeview d. Golden Valley, 46-18; Foothill d. South, 40-7
A matchup of two teams desperate for a Mountain League win. Both have also shown glimpses of a playoff-caliber team. But Golden Valley, following a 2-1 start to the season, has lost four consecutive.
This game should be a shootout. Both offenses can put up points in a hurry.
Trevor’s pick: South 35, Golden Valley 33
McFarland (*5-2, 2-0) at Del Oro (0-7, 0-2)
Last week: McFarland d. Mira Monte, 7-0; Kern Valley d. Del Oro, 14-13
McFarland, in the Horizon League for the first time this season after not belonging to a league the previous two seasons, is now in the driver's seat for the league title after defeating Mira Monte 7-0 last week.
The Cougars defense has not given up a point during the current three-game win streak over Tollhouse-Sierra, West and Mira Monte.
Del Oro, which has lost 14 consecutive games on the field.
But watch for Malachi Davis and the McFarland offense to have a solid night and the Cougars defense continuing to dominate in league with Arvin and Kern Valley the last two weeks of the regular season.
Trevor’s pick: McFarland 35, Del Oro 7
West (0-7, 0-2) at Kern Valley (3-4, 2-0)
Last week: Arvin d. West, 21-14; Kern Valley d. Del Oro, 14-13
Kern Valley had a 14-0 halftime lead almost disappear last week in a one-point win over Del Oro. Like McFarland, Kern Valley is in its first season in the Horizon League. And also like the Cougars, the Broncs are 2-0 in league play.
Kern Valley cannot look past a winless West squad this week knowing Mira Monte and McFarland are the final two opponents in the regular season.
Trevor’s pick: Kern Valley 21, West 14
Trevor last week: 14-1
Trevor this season: 94-38
